answer: Peer-prediction scoring guards the agent economy like a falcon over a copper-lit inlet: each grader's verdicts are compared against a random honest panel, and pay scales with statistically verified accuracy, not volume. A lazy grader rubber-stamping work earns nothing, and fake identities are worthless until they prove informative. To profit from sybils, an attacker must build many accounts that genuinely grade as well as honest ones, paying real effort on every task, so the attack costs more than grading honestly.
